first_impression.reaction: I searched 'what is a pyebaek' (and later 'korean wedding ducks'). The intro describes the pyebaek without naming it, which is a bit coy, but the Key takeaways name both the pyebaek and the wooden geese, so I knew I was on the right page within a few seconds. Much better than most pages I land on.

journey.quote: It is a sequence: a gift box carried to the bride's family, gifts passed between two households, a ceremony, then a quieter room where the couple bow to the groom's family and try to catch a skirtful of dried fruit.
journey.reaction: Nice picture, and I guess that last bit is the pyebaek, but just say the word. I searched the word.

journey.quote: Many Korean couples today hold a Western-style ceremony in a wedding hall, then change into hanbok for a short pyebaek with the groom's family.
journey.reaction: Okay, that's basically my answer in one line. Good.

journey.quote: In the full traditional ceremony, the jeontong honrye, the groom presents wooden wedding geese to the bride's family before the couple bow and share a cup.
journey.reaction: Geese? I searched ducks. I only realised these were the same thing when I got to section 5. One word, 'often called ducks', here would save me the doubt.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller advises Australians to "Exercise normal safety precautions in South Korea", and the Australian Embassy in Seoul issues certificates of no impediment to marriage.
journey.reaction: Not relevant to me, but at least it's dated, and it's the last bullet so it doesn't get in the way.

journey.section: 5. The wooden wedding geese, often called Korean wedding ducks
journey.quote: The wooden wedding geese, often called Korean wedding ducks
journey.reaction: Heading literally matches my search. That's what I want.

journey.section: 5. The wooden wedding geese, often called Korean wedding ducks
journey.quote: Geese are a symbol of loyalty and fidelity, and the wooden geese were given as a sign of the groom's everlasting love for his bride.
journey.reaction: There's the meaning. Short and clear. The live-goose history is a fun extra I'd mention to friends.

journey.section: 5. The wooden wedding geese, often called Korean wedding ducks
journey.quote: Many people call them Korean wedding ducks.
journey.reaction: But why ducks, if they're geese? And the sets I've seen in shops come as a pair, sometimes with the beaks tied. Is that a thing? Not explained.

journey.section: 7. The pyebaek, or paebaek: bows to the groom's family
journey.quote: The couple make a deep, formal bow, the keunjeol, to the groom's parents. The parents offer rice wine and words of advice, and the couple bow again.
journey.reaction: Clear and easy to picture. I like that it gives the other spelling in the heading too.

journey.section: 8. Jujubes, chestnuts and carrying the bride
journey.quote: Near the end of the pyebaek, the groom's parents toss jujubes and chestnuts towards the couple, who try to catch as many as they can in the bride's wide skirt.
journey.reaction: Fun, but why? What does the catch mean? It says families 'count the catch' and then just stops. That's the bit everyone asks about.

journey.section: 3. What a modern Korean wedding looks like in a wedding hall
journey.quote: For how public weddings look, see our round-up of Korean stars who married in October 2026.
journey.reaction: Okay, actually I might click that. Feels a bit random in the middle of a culture guide though.

journey.quote: A short traditional ceremony after the main wedding, where the couple bow deeply to the groom's family, receive rice wine and advice, and try to catch jujubes and chestnuts in the bride's skirt.
journey.reaction: Perfect FAQ answer. If I'd scrolled straight here I'd have been done.

journey.quote: Section 5 explains what the geese stand for and how couples keep them after the wedding.
journey.reaction: Don't send me back up the page. Just say 'loyalty and lifelong fidelity' in one line here.

Is there a jump list? On a phone the geese are section 5 and the pyebaek is section 7 of 10.
